Ability.description:
One thing glave can do with a connected host. Whether an action runs without asking is
still for approvals to say (`approvals.md`).

oneOf.description: Read and clone the repositories it reaches.
Push branches to them.
Open and comment on pull requests (merge requests on GitLab).
Open and comment on issues.

AcceptedPasskeys.description:
Every passkey that signs the person in with a relying party, after a sign-in, for the
browser to tell its passkey manager (`PublicKeyCredential.signalAllAcceptedCredentials`),
which then hides or deletes the person's others there.

credentials.description: Each passkey's credential id (`allAcceptedCredentialIds`), in base64url.

party.description: The relying party's id (`rpId`): the public origin's name, or `localhost`.

user.description: The person's user handle (`userId`), in base64url.

Answer.description: The person's answer to an approval.

ApiError.description: A request that failed, as JSON-RPC carries it.

message.description: What a person is told, in their language where it is the server's own sentence.

At.description:
When an event was recorded, in UTC at millisecond precision. For people only: events are
ordered by [`Seq`]. Always written with three fractional digits, such as
`2026-10-07T21:14:01.250Z`, so every instant has exactly one spelling.

AttachedFile.description: A file `turn/start` adds to its message: one `file/upload` kept in the thread's project.

name.description: Its name, shown with the message and told to the model.

AwakeInfo.description:
Whether this server keeps its computer from sleeping on its own while a turn, task or
schedule runs (`specs/one-server.md`, owner decision 10).

oneOf.description: Never: a server, which does not sleep. There is nothing to choose.

On a person's own computer, as they choose: kept awake while glave works when `on`, the
screen still free to sleep and closing the lid still sleeping it.

On a person's own computer that glave has nothing to keep awake with: why, in a
sentence.

CallId.description: Links a tool call to its result: 1 to 128 printable ASCII characters.

CallRun.description:
Tool calls one after another in a turn, with nothing said between them: no message with
words, and no questions for the person.

sentence.description:
What they did, in a line: "Ran 2 commands (1 failed)", "Ran 1 command, read 1 file";
in the present while one of them runs.

ChangeKind.description: What a change did to its file.

oneOf.description: Wrote the whole file (`write`).
Swapped one piece for another (`edit`).
Swapped every match of a piece (`edit` with `replace_all`).

ChangedFile.description: A file, with every line its changes added and took out, and each change.

path.description: Where it is, as the call named it.

Checkout.description: Where a folder is checked out: a computer, and the path on it.

computer.description: The computer, by the id it keeps across runs.

path.description: The folder's absolute path there, links resolved.

CommandId.description:
Identifies a command kept running in the background, unique everywhere (UUID v7, minted by
the computer it runs on).

ComputerId.description: Identifies a computer, unique everywhere (UUID v7, minted by the adapter that made it).

ComputerKind.description: What kind of computer it is.

oneOf.description: The machine glave runs on.
A computer glave made elsewhere, such as a cloud worker.

The person's own computer in the cloud, which glave wakes and puts to sleep, keeping
its disk.

ComputerRef.description: The computer a workspace is on.

ConnectionInfo.description: A connection's sign-in to its remote MCP server, or a server that asks for one.

name.description: What the person's settings call the server at that address, when they name one.

usage.description: How much it was used, once it is in the person's settings.

ConnectionStatus.description: Whether the person is signed in, and the sign-in still works.

oneOf.description: Its token works, or renews before it expires.

Its token works, but its server asked for more than it grants (`403
insufficient_scope`): the person signs in again, for all of it.
Its token expired with nothing to renew it: the person signs in again.
Not signed in: one of the person's remote servers, which asks them to sign in.

ContextUse.description:
How full a thread's context is: what its conversation last sent and got back, of the window
compaction aims for.

percent.description:
`tokens` of `window`, in whole percent, at most 100. A turn compacts before a request
past its threshold (80 unless set).

tokens.description: The tokens its latest call sent and got back.

window.description:
The window compaction aims for, in tokens: the configured one, or a smaller one the
model stated.

CredentialId.description:
Identifies one sign-in a person keeps, sealed under a key of its own: a git host
(`credential.connected`) or a connection (`connection.connected`).

CredentialInfo.description: A git host the person connected.

can.description:
What glave can do with it, from what the host said the token may do; absent when the
host did not say, so a client claims nothing.

expired.description:
Its sign-in has expired, with nothing left to renew it: only signing in again brings it
back.

login.description: Whom the host said the token is for, when it said.

balance.description:
What is left: everything added, less everything charged. Below nothing only where a
call to a model with no price spent past it.

limit.description: The most it may spend in a month, when anything limits it.

spent.description: What it spent this month, glave's own work in it included.

CreditsInfo.description: An organization's credits, as much of them as the caller may see.

account.description: The organization's own account, for its Owners and Admins; none for anyone else.

can_set_limit.description: Whether the caller may set the month's limit (`credits/limit`): its Owners.

people.description:
What each person spent this month, most first: everyone who spent anything, for its
Owners and Admins; for anyone else, the caller alone.

since.description: When this month began, in UTC: what the month's spending counts from.

Currency.description: An ISO 4217 currency code: three uppercase ASCII letters, such as `USD`.

DeviceCode.description:
Signing in to GitHub in the browser (its device flow): the person opens `url` and enters
`code`, then the client waits on `flow` with `credential/device/poll`.

code.description: What the person enters on GitHub's page, such as `WDJB-MJHT`.

url.description: GitHub's page where the code is entered.

EndpointInfo.description:
One provider serving a model through a router, as the router says, for a client to filter
and choose by. What the router does not say is absent, never guessed.

based_in.description:
The country it is based in, an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as `US`, when the router
says.

context.description: The context window this provider serves the model with, in tokens.

datacenters.description:
The countries its datacenters are in, when the router says; absent when it does not,
which says nothing of where they are.

hidden_by.description:
Which of the caller's filters hide it (`filters/get`), so no call of theirs goes to it;
none when it fits them all.

keeps_nothing.description:
Whether it keeps nothing of what it is sent (zero data retention). Every provider
that serves glave through a router is one that never trains on it.

max_output.description: The longest answer this provider gives, in tokens.

precision.description: How precisely it serves the model's weights.

slug.description: What a person's filters name it by, such as `deepinfra`.

speed.description:
How many tokens a second it answered with: the router's median over the half hour
before its catalog was read, when it says.

anyOf.description: Why a model call failed, for a client to say what to fix.
anyOf.title: ModelFailure

anyOf.description: The passkey a browser signed in with that the server does not know.
anyOf.title: UnknownPasskeyFailure

ErrorData.description: What a failure says beyond its sentence, for a client to act on.

Exists.description:
What a server has beyond a person's own: each because its configuration provides it, never
a setting naming a kind of deployment (`specs/deployments.md`, "One code path"). A client
draws only what is here, and nothing of what is not.

credits.description:
Credits: each organization pays ahead for what it uses, and its model calls are
charged to them (`credits/get`). Absent where they are not, so what a server that
keeps none says is as it was.

organization.description: An organization of people, who sign in through its identity provider (OIDC).

workers.description: Workers: a fresh machine for each thread of the project whose settings chose them.

Failure.description: The kind of a failed model request.

oneOf.description: The key was refused (401, 403), or credentials could not be had.
The account has no credit left (402).
The server has no such model, or no chat completions API at that address.
The conversation is longer than the model's context window.
The provider is limiting requests (429).
The provider failed on its side (5xx).
The server could not be reached, or the connection broke.
The server sent nothing for too long.
The server's answer did not follow the protocol.
Any other refusal of the request.
The call could exceed a budget, so it was not sent.

FileChange.description:
One change to a file: a `write` or an `edit` that finished without an error, as its call
asked for it, which the tool applied exactly.

lines.description:
Its lines in order: those kept before it, those taken out, those put in, and those kept
after it.

FileInfo.description: A file the server keeps, as `file/upload` answers it.

media_type.description: Its media type, such as `image/png`, as what it holds says.

name.description: Its name, as the person's computer called it.

sha256.description: Its content's SHA-256, which `turn/start` names it by.

Filters.description:
A person's filters among the providers a router passes their calls on to. What is not
chosen does not filter.

avoid.description: Providers never to use, by slug.

based_in.description:
Only providers based in these countries (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes), each of their
datacenters too where the router names them; anywhere when none.

keeps_nothing.description: Only providers that keep nothing of what they are sent (zero data retention).

max_price.description: The most a provider's tokens may cost.

precision.description:
The least precision a provider may serve a model's weights at; a provider that does
not say its precision serves no filter but none.

serves.description:
Who serves a model, by the model's id, where the person chose for it apart from
`sort`.

sort.description:
Which provider to prefer when several may serve: the router's own balance unless
chosen.

FolderSource.description: Where a folder's files come from.

oneOf.description: A git repository, by the address it is cloned from: where the folder comes back from.
A folder on a computer, with no repository it comes from: only its checkout has it.

Forge.description:
Which forge a git host runs, as far as glave could tell: what its API and its
command-line tool are.

oneOf.description: GitHub, or GitHub Enterprise Server: `gh`.
GitLab, its own or self-managed: `glab`.
Gitea or Forgejo: `tea`.
Bitbucket Cloud.
Any other host git reaches over HTTPS.

GoalProgress.description: A thread's latest goal and how far it has come.

ended.description: Why it ended; `None` while it is active.

note.description: When it is paused, what the model needs from the person, in its words.

tokens.description: Tokens its turns have used so far.

oneOf.description: The model verified the goal is met and said so with `update_goal`.

The model cannot go on without the person, and said why with `update_goal`. The goal
can be resumed.
The person stopped it, or cancelled its turn.
Its token budget ran out.
Three turns in a row ended without the model calling a tool: no progress.

GoneFolder.description:
A project whose folder isn't there anymore, on the computer it is checked out on, with the
sentence that says so.

Grouping.description:
How a client groups the person's threads: each under its project, or each under what it is
doing (waiting for the person, running, idle).

Hides.description: A filter of a person's that hides a provider of a model.

oneOf.description:
It is based, or runs, outside the countries chosen, or the router does not say where
it is based.
It serves the model's weights at less than the precision chosen, or does not say.
It may keep what it is sent, where only providers that keep nothing are chosen.
Its tokens cost more than the most chosen, or the router does not say what they cost.
The person chose to avoid it.

IdempotencyKey.description: A client's name for one attempt at a turn: 1 to 255 bytes of text.

InviteId.description: Identifies one invite to an organization (`specs/model.md`, "Invites").

InviteInfo.description: An invite waiting to be opened. Its code is never shown again after it is made.

email.description: The address its link was emailed to, when it was.

expires.description: When it stops working, opened or not.

role.description: The role it gives whoever opens it.

JoinWay.description: How the one who holds an invite joins the organization it is to.

oneOf.description: Not signed in: by making a passkey, a new glave account.
Not signed in: by signing in through the organization's company login.
Signed in: by accepting it, the organization one more of theirs.
Signed in, and in the organization already: nothing to join.

LineKind.description: Whether a line was kept, taken out or put in.

LinkKind.description: Which link's code a passkey is made with (`passkey/create_options`).

oneOf.description: A setup link from glave on the server's computer: the local person's passkey.
An invite's: the first passkey of a new account, joining its organization.
A sign-up's, emailed: the first passkey of a new account and its own organization.
One to get back in, emailed: a new passkey for the account the address has.

MaxPrice.description: The most a provider's tokens may cost, in millionths of a US dollar per million tokens.

MemoryId.description: Identifies one memory: a short statement kept for later threads (`specs/memory.md`).

MemoryScope.description: Where a memory belongs: to the person, or to the project it was saved in.

oneOf.description: About the person: read in their threads, in projects that allow it.
About the project's work, in a project that is the person's own: read only in its threads.

MemorySource.description: Where in a thread a memory was saved.

Meta.description: What a request may carry besides its params, in `params._meta`.

idempotency_key.description:
For `turn/start`: the same key for the same thread returns the turn already started
instead of starting another, so a client may retry safely.

traceparent.description:
For `turn/start`: the W3C trace the turn belongs to (`00-<trace id>-<parent id>-<flags>`),
recorded with the turn and joined by glave's spans. One that is not one is ignored.

ModelInfo.description: One model a thread may be sent to.

default.description: Whether threads that choose no model use this one. Exactly one model is the default.

endpoints.description:
Each provider that serves it through a router (OpenRouter), as the router's catalog
lists them; none where no router serves it.

id.description: What `thread/start` and `turn/start` take as `model`: the name the gateway knows it by.

maker.description:
Who made it, such as `Anthropic`: as its provider says, else from its id's prefix
(`anthropic/…`); absent when neither says.

max_output.description: The longest answer it gives, in tokens.

name.description:
Its own name, without its maker's, such as `Claude Haiku 5.5`: the settings', else its
provider's, else written from its id as its maker writes it.

price.description: What its tokens cost at the first of its providers.

providers.description:
The services that run it, in a person's words (`OpenRouter`, `Anthropic`, a server's
address), in the order glave tries them: the first, then each after it only when the
one before fails.

reasoning.description:
How it reasons, when it can: the levels of effort it offers, in its provider's names,
and as `default` the level its first provider is sent when a thread chooses none, the
one that provider's catalog says the model uses unasked. No `default` when glave sends
none, and the model reasons as its maker set it.

Money.description:
An exact amount: `micros` millionths of one unit of `currency`. `{"micros": 4200,
"currency": "USD"}` is $0.0042.

NewFolder.description: A new project's folder, on the computer glave runs on.

oneOf.description: A folder already on this computer, by its full path: worked in where it is.

A repository cloned onto this computer, from its `https://` address, signing in with
the git host connected for it.
A new, empty folder, made a git repository.
A folder worked on in place.
A git worktree of the repository at `repository`, on its own `branch`.

A repository cloned into a new copy, at a branch, tag or commit (its default branch
when absent).
A folder of the thread's own, for a thread with no project.

OrgRole.description: What a person may do in their organization. A person given no role is a Member.

oneOf.description: Uses glave within what is granted.
Manages people, policy, the approved connections, models, the budget and audit.
Everything, billing and ownership included.

OrganizationInfo.description: An organization the caller belongs to, as it is to them.

current.description: Whether this request works in it.

id.description: Its id, which a request names in `Glave-Organization` to work in it.

name.description:
What it is called: "Personal" for the caller's own; another, while organizations have
no names of their own, by an Owner of it ("Dana Lee's team"), else "A team".

own.description:
Whether it is the caller's own: the one they signed up into, or for the person on the
server's computer, the server's own.

people.description: How many people are in it, the person on the server's computer counted in its own.

Origin.description: What started a thread, and who.

by.description: Who started it, when that differs from the thread's `for`.

ref.description: An opaque pointer to what started it, such as a schedule or a chat thread.

OriginKind.description: What kind of thing started a thread.

PasskeySummary.description: A passkey that signs the person in.

current.description: Whether it signed in the browser asking.

emailed.description: Whether it was made from a link sent to the account's email, to get back in.

name.description: What it is called: the name the browser gave it, else when it was added.

used.description: When it last signed a browser in.

PayloadVersion.description: The version of one payload type, starting at 1.

Permissions.description:
What the agent may do without asking the person (`specs/approvals.md`, "Modes"): the one
choice a person makes about it, its mode. Ordered by caution, the most cautious least, so a
policy's cap is the highest mode it allows. Each comes to a sandbox and how much asks
wherever it runs (`glave-harness`). The names from before the modes were renamed (#739),
`read-only` and `workspace`, still read as `ask` and `auto`, so logs and files written then
still open; only the new names are written.

oneOf.description:
Plan: the agent looks around and proposes a plan, and changes nothing until the person
approves it: commands run in the sandbox that writes nothing of the project, and what
Ask first would ask about is refused instead.

Ask first: commands run in a sandbox that writes nothing of the project, and every
change asks first.

The agent works on its own in the project, or the chat's folder: commands run in the
sandbox and nothing inside it asks; risky actions ask or go to the judge. Where no
sandbox can run, every change and command asks instead.

No sandbox, and nothing ever asks, risky actions included; what would show the model a
secret is declined instead. For work the person fully trusts.

PersonInfo.description: A person who signed in through the organization's identity provider.

email.description: Their email, as the identity provider's token said it, when it did.

groups.description: The identity provider's groups they were in when they last signed in.

joined.description:
When they first signed in; none for the person on the server's computer, who never
joins: they own its organization.

local.description: Whether they are the person on the server's computer, its organization's owner always.

name.description:
Their name: as the identity provider's token said it, when it did, or as they gave it
with a glave account.

removable.description: Whether the caller may take them out of the organization.

roles.description:
The roles the caller may give them now, theirs among them; none when the caller may
not change their role.

subject.description: Who they are to the company login: its id for them; none with a glave account.

PersonSpent.description: What one person spent this month.

name.description: The name the organization knows them by, else their email, when it knows either.

PlanInfo.description: A thread's plan: its latest `plan.updated`, by the model or the person.

proposed.description:
Whether it waits for the person: proposed in plan mode and not approved yet, to build
(`plan/build`), edit (`plan/edit`) or change with a message.

sentence.description: What it is, in a sentence: "Proposed plan: 5 steps", "Plan: 2 of 5 steps done".

steps.description: The steps, in order, each with its status.

PlanStatus.description: How far a step has come: to do, doing, done.

step.description: What to do, in a line.

Precision.description: How precisely a provider serves a model's weights, from how it says they are stored.

oneOf.description: It does not say.
Four bits a weight: `int4`, `fp4`, `mxfp4`, `nvfp4`.
Six bits a weight: `fp6`.
Eight bits a weight: `int8`, `fp8`, `mxfp8`.
The weights as they were trained: `fp16`, `bf16`, `fp32`.

Principal.description:
A reference to a principal: `{"kind": "person", "id": "…"}`. Every kind but `glave` has an
id.

PrincipalId.description:
Identifies a principal: a person, an agent profile or a group. People, agents and groups
share one id space, unique everywhere and never tied to one deployment.

Project.description: A project, as its record keeps it.

owner.description: Whose it is: a person, or later a team or an agent. Only they work in it.

ProjectFolder.description: A project's folder: where its files come from, and where they are checked out.

ProjectId.description: Identifies a project: the boundary for memory, history, files and policy.

oneOf.description: A project: its owner's work, usually tied to a folder.

A person's own project: their one-off chats and their personal memory. Each
person has exactly one in each organization.

ProviderId.description: Identifies one model account a person connected (`provider.connected`).

ProviderInfo.description: A model account the person connected.

models.description: The models it offers, the one glave uses by default first.

url.description: The server's API, for a `compatible` account.

ProviderKind.description: Which service a model account is with.

oneOf.description: Any other server that speaks OpenAI's API, at a URL the person gives.

multiple.description: Whether more than one choice may be picked.

options.description: Choices to pick from; the person may answer in their own words either way.

QueuedMessage.description: A message queued to the turn running in its thread, for the model's next call.

id.description:
The id of the `message.added` it is recorded as once the model reads it: that
`thread/event` says it was read. A `turn/live` `unread` with this id says it never will be.

RawEvent.description:
An event exactly as it is stored and sent. `data` holds the payload's bytes as written;
[`crate::decode`] interprets them.

Reasoning.description: How a model reasons: the levels of effort it offers, in its service's own names.

default.description: The level it uses when none is asked for, one of `efforts`, when its service says.

efforts.description:
The levels it offers, as its service lists them, such as `high`, `medium`, `low`, and
`none` where reasoning can be turned off. Empty when it offers no choice.

Remembered.description: One memory as it is shown: to the model, and to the person.

source.description: The thread and `seq` it was saved in.

untrusted_read.description: Saved in a thread that had read untrusted content or a secrets file.

version.description: 1 when saved, one more with each edit.

RememberingInfo.description: Whether glave remembers for the person (`specs/memory.md`, "Defaults and policy").

oneOf.description:
Not the caller's to choose here, and `reason`, why: their organization turned memory
off, or only the person on this computer chooses.
The person's to turn on or off: on when `on`.

ReplySources.description:
The pages one reply drew on: each one its turn read with `web_fetch` before it, once, in the
order first read. A page that failed to load is none, nor is a search's result the agent
did not read.

pages.description: The pages, in the order the turn first read each.

reply.description: The `seq` of the reply's `message.added`: the last words of its turn.

sentence.description: What they are, in a sentence: "Sources: 3 pages".

RunningCommand.description:
A command a thread keeps running in the background, as a client lists it: what it runs,
since when, and a sentence saying so (`command/list`).

command.description: What it runs, as the agent wrote it.

started_at.description: When it started, once the thread has recorded it.

summary.description: What it is doing, in plain words.

ScheduleId.description: Identifies one schedule: a prompt or goal that runs as a task at set times.

last.description: When it last ran: the time that run was due.

next.description: When it runs next; absent once a one-off has run.

SearchInfo.description: Whether the person's agent may search the web (`specs/session.md`, "Web search").

oneOf.description:
Not the caller's to choose here, and `reason`, why: their organization chooses its
search among its approved connections, this server keeps no connections of the
person's own, or only the person on its computer chooses.

The person's to turn on or off: on when `on`; `detail` says who searches and what it
costs; `usage`, while it is on and when asked for, how much it searched this month.

Secret.description: A key or token: sent once, never shown again.

Seq.description:
An event's position in its thread, starting at 1 and assigned gap-free by the thread's
single writer. This is the order of events; time never is.

Serve.description: Who serves one model, as a person chose.

oneOf.description: Whichever provider within the filters is cheapest, or fastest, when it is called.
This provider alone, by slug.

email.description:
Whether it sends email (`[email]`) with links to its public origin, as an invite's: so
a client asks for an address only where one is used.

exists.description:
What it has beyond the one person a server works for on its own; absent where it has
none of it, as on a person's own computer or server.

here.description:
Where a browser on this computer makes and signs in with passkeys, when the server
makes them here rather than at a public origin: `http://localhost:<port>`.

id.description:
The server's id, where it signs browsers in: the same across restarts, and the one a
browser's session must name before the browser presents it.

invites.description:
Whether the caller may invite someone here: the server takes invites (glave accounts
at a public origin, or a company login), and the caller's role permits it. So a person
alone, whose organization is shown to no one, can still make the first.

modes.description:
The modes a thread may choose (`permissions` on `thread/start` and `turn/start`):
those the policy leaves, in the order a person is offered them, the recommended first.

origin.description: Where people reach the server from elsewhere, if they do: its public origin.

permissions.description:
What the agent may do in a thread that, and whose project, chose no mode:
`--permissions` or `permissions` in `config.toml` (`specs/approvals.md`, "Modes").

role.description:
The caller's role in the organization, when there is one and they signed in: so a
client shows admin screens only to its Admins and Owners. Absent on a server with no
organization, where the one person may do everything.

signin.description:
How a browser signs in to it; none where no browser does, as over stdio. A passkey: at a
public origin always, a setup link making the first; on this computer once one is made.

unsandboxed.description:
Why Auto asks before every change and command here, in a sentence, when it does:
no sandbox can run on this computer (Ask first then asks so too), or only one that keeps
files as they are.

Setting.description: A person's own settings or connections, by what a client reads to show them.

oneOf.description:
Their model accounts (`provider/list`), and so the models threads may choose
(`model/list`).
Their git hosts (`credential/list`).
Their sign-ins to connections (`connection/list`).
Whether their agent may search the web (`search/get`).
How their clients group their threads (`grouping/get`).
Their filters among a router's providers (`filters/get`).
Whether the computer is kept awake while glave works (`awake/get`).
Whether glave remembers for them (`memory/get`).
Their passkeys (`passkey/list`).

The language the server writes its own sentences to them in (`language/get`): what a
client shows of the server's words, an approval's included, it reads again.
Threads that are neither archived nor deleted.
Deleted threads, waiting for their content to be erased: for the operator that does it.

ShownInvite.description: What an invite's link opens, for whoever holds it: never its code, nor whom it was sent to.

by.description:
Who made it, by the name the organization knows them by, else their email; none for
the person who runs this glave, who has neither here.

organization.description: The organization it is to, for a client to work in once its person joins.

SignInLink.description:
Signing in to a remote server in the browser: the person opens `url`, its authorization server's
page, then the client waits on `flow` with `connection/poll`.

url.description: The page where the person signs in and approves glave.

SignInWay.description: A way a browser signs in to the server, as `server/discover` says.

oneOf.description: A link glave on the server's own computer makes, good once, for a browser there.

A passkey: at the server's public origin, where a setup link from glave on its computer
makes the first; or on this computer, once a browser signed in by glave's link made one.

Signing up with an email: a link sent there makes the person's first passkey, their
account and an organization of their own.

Getting back in by email: a link sent to a glave account's address makes a new passkey
for it.

Sort.description: Which of a model's providers a router prefers.

oneOf.description: The lowest price.
The most tokens a second.

Standing.description:
Whether a thread is shown: the latest `thread.archived`, `thread.unarchived` or
`thread.deleted` decides.

oneOf.description: Shown in lists.
Hidden from lists and kept in the log; `unarchive` brings it back.
Hidden for good, and waiting for its content to be erased.

A turn is paused until someone answers an approval or a question, or the thread's
project asks the person to trust it.

TaskInfo.description: A task, as the tasks panel shows it.

budget.description: Tokens the run may use; no limit when absent.

cost.description: What they cost so far, when every call reported a cost.

elapsed_ms.description: Milliseconds from its start until now, or until it ended.

outcome.description: How it ended, once it has.

project.description: The project its thread is in.

schedule.description: The schedule that started it, if one did.

tokens.description: Tokens used so far, subagents' included.

TaskKind.description: What kind of work a task is. Background commands the model starts arrive later.

oneOf.description: A thread: a turn, or a goal's turns, run by the agent.

TaskStatus.description: Whether a task is still going.

oneOf.description: Started and not ended, by a server other than this one (or one that stopped).

ThreadChanges.description: The files a thread changed, its subagents' changes with its own, and each turn's.

files.description: Every file it changed, in the order first changed.

note.description:
What they leave out, in a sentence: "Changes made by commands or other tools are not
listed."

turns.description: Each turn that changed files, in order.

ThreadId.description: Identifies one thread: a conversation or task with its own ordered log.

ThreadSteps.description: Each run of a thread's tool calls, and its turns' replies.

replies.description:
The `seq` of each reply: the last `message.added` of the model's with words in a turn
that ended. Every other message of the model's is said along the way.

runs.description: Each run of calls, in order.

ThreadSummary.description: A thread, as a list shows it: from the threads view, with what it is doing now.

context.description:
How full its context is, as compaction measures it; absent before its first model call
and since it was compacted.

cost.description:
What they cost, when every call reported a cost; absent when one did not: the cost is
not reported.

estimated.description:
True when a usage count in `tokens`, and so `cost`, was estimated: a stream ended before
its provider reported it.

for.description: Whose work it is; absent in threads from before it was recorded (the local person).

parent.description: The thread whose call started this one, for a subagent's.

permissions.description:
What the agent may do in its next turn: the mode last chosen for it, else its
project's, else the server's.

title.description: The title the person gave it, else the first line of their first message.

tokens.description: Tokens its own model calls used.

trust.description:
What its project asks the person on this computer to trust, once the thread was opened
or started: shown to them alone, until they answer it.

workspace.description:
Where it works, once it has a workspace, as its latest `workspace.bound` records it: the
computer (the one the server runs on, or a worker), the folder its tools act in, and how
it got it (its project's folder in place, a worktree on a branch of its own, a clone, or
a scratch folder).

TokenCounts.description:
Token counts as inclusive totals with subsets: `input` includes `cache_read` and
`cache_write`, and `output` includes `reasoning`. Providers disagree on what their totals
include, so adapters normalize before writing.

TokenPrice.description: What a model's tokens cost, in millionths of a US dollar per million tokens.

cache_read.description: Input read from the service's cache, when it prices that apart.

TrustAsk.description:
What a thread's project brings that runs only once the person on this computer trusts it:
its tool servers, its hooks and settings that loosen how its commands run
(`specs/policy.md`, "Project trust").

ask.description:
Names exactly what is asked: `trust/answer` names it back, so only what the person was
shown is trusted.

items.description: Each thing in plain words, in the order the project lists them.

TrustChoice.description: The person's answer to a project's ask.

oneOf.description: Everything the ask listed is on from the thread's next turn, and the answer is kept.
It stays off, nothing is kept, and this thread stops asking.

TrustItem.description: One thing a project brings, in plain words.

detail.description:
The thing itself, when there is one to show: the command it runs, the address, the
model.

text.description: What it does, in a sentence: `Runs a tool server`.

TurnResult.description:
A turn ended (`turn.ended`): how, and what it did and cost, its subagents' work included.
It is what a client that ran the turn is answered with too, so every client reads the same.
A turn recorded before it held more than `outcome` reads with nothing counted.

changed.description:
The files its `write` and `edit` calls changed, each once in the order first changed,
as the call named it: what `thread/changes` gives as the turn's, so a client keeps their
room before it has read them. Absent when it changed none.

cost.description:
What its model calls cost, when every one of them reported a cost in one currency;
absent when one did not: the cost is not reported.

estimated.description:
True when a usage count was estimated, because a stream ended before the provider
reported it.

outside_sandbox.description: The commands that ran outside the sandbox, each one allowed.

via.description:
Where its model calls ran, once each in the order they first did, in a person's words:
the service, and the provider a service that routes calls passed them on to
(`OpenRouter (Anthropic)`).

with_network.description:
The commands that ran with the network the sandbox otherwise kept from them, each one
allowed.

TypeName.description:
What happened: lowercase dotted segments such as `tool.call.requested`, at most 64 bytes.
Each segment is lowercase ASCII letters, digits and underscores; the name starts with a
letter.

UnknownPasskey.description:
A passkey a browser signed in with that the server does not know, removed since the
sign-in began, for the browser to tell its passkey manager
(`PublicKeyCredential.signalUnknownCredential`), which then deletes it.

Update.description: Progress while a turn runs: the live side of `Live`, in a form any transport carries.

oneOf.description:
The reasoning's headline changed: its last bold title, else its last whole sentence, as
the model wrote it. A client shows the latest one beside the word that it thinks.

The reasoning ended after `ms` milliseconds: the model wrote something else, or its call
ended. Its message records the same (`message.added`'s `thought`).

An action that did not run. `summary` is what would have run; `caution`, why it asked,
in sentences the person reads, when a caution did: in the caller's language where it
was recorded with its reason.

A model call began, and nothing has come back yet: each step of a turn starts with
one, so text and reasoning after it are the new step's, and what streamed before it
from a call that was not recorded (one tried again) is gone.
The model asked the person questions; answer with `question/answer`.

The `approval.requested` of call `approval` waits for an answer; give it with
`approval/decide`. One the judge let run is decided at once and sends none.
A subagent started; its notifications follow under its own thread.
A subagent is done; `ok` when it finished its work.

A message sent while the turn ran (its `queued` id) that the model will not read, given
back: a hook stopped it (`reason`, the hook's), or the turn was stopped or failed first.
A memory was saved, edited or forgotten: `change` is `remembered`, `edited` or `forgot`.

Usage.description: How much a connection was used since this month began (UTC).

calls.description: The calls the person's agent asked of its tools, refused ones too.

sentence.description:
The calls, as the person reads them: "412 calls this month", or for web search "412
searches this month".

oneOf.description: The client ended it.
The thread was deleted: nothing more will be recorded in it.

WebPage.description:
A web page a call read (`web_fetch`), as its `tool.call.completed` records it in

title.description: The title the page gives itself, when it gives one.

url.description: Where it was found, after redirects.

oneOf.description: Once, at this time.
Whenever this five-field cron expression matches, in UTC.

WorkspaceBound.description: The thread's tools act in this workspace from now on.

root.description:
The workspace root, an absolute path as the computer names it. Tool output and glave's
own fields use paths relative to it.

workspace.description: The workspace's id, as its computer named it.

description: JSON-RPC 2.0 methods, notifications and errors of glave's session API (specs/session.md). Generated from the Rust protocol types by `cargo xtask schema`; do not edit.

ARCHIVED.message: The thread is archived; unarchive it first

HOST.message: The git host, or a connection's server or its sign-in, refused or could not be reached

INVALID_REQUEST.message: The message is not a valid request

MEMORY_OFF.message: Memory is off for this server

NOT_ALLOWED.message: The caller may not do this

NOT_AVAILABLE.message: Not available yet, such as a thread on a computer of the person's own

NO_COMMAND.message: No such command is running in the background in this thread

NO_CREDENTIAL.message: No such git host, connection or sign-in here

NO_FILE.message: No such file here: never kept in this project, or no message used it within a day

NO_FOLDER.message: The project's folder isn't there anymore: give it its new place (`project/folder/set`) or remove the project (`project/remove`)

NO_GOAL.message: The thread has no active goal (or, to resume, no paused one)

NO_IMAGES.message: The thread's model does not read images

NO_INVITE.message: No such invite waits here: it was used, revoked or has expired, or it is another organization's

NO_MODEL.message: No such model here, or not one this server may run

NO_ORGANIZATION.message: No organization by that id is on this server

NO_PERSON.message: No one by that id has signed in to this organization

NO_PLAN.message: The thread has no plan waiting for the person's approval

NO_SERVER.message: No remote server of the person's settings goes by that name or address

NO_TRUST.message: No such ask waits: the project changed since, or asks nothing now

NO_TURN.message: No turn is running in this thread

QUEUE_FULL.message: As many messages wait for the running turn as it takes

RUNNING_ELSEWHERE.message: The thread is working on another server, which holds it

server's `modes`. The thread's latest choice when absent, else its project's, else
the server's. Not while a turn runs.

unattended.description:
No one answers the turn it starts: what would ask is declined at once and
`question` is not offered, as in a task, for its subagents too, while it still
streams to whoever follows it. For a client with no one at it, such as a script.
